title: TypeScript SDK: sum-type adapters + Zod/JSON-Schema codegen and streaming examples
creator: Maya Chen
description: Add first-class support in the TypeScript SDK for generating runtime validators and schema artifacts from model output contracts: (1) codegen Zod schemas and JSON-Schema for discriminated/sum types, (2) produce ergonomic TypeScript union types and type guards, and (3) provide streaming parsing helpers that yield partial union variants as tokens arrive. This improves safety for structured output, simplifies user code, and enables better error handling and retries when streaming outputs are ambiguous or truncated.
background: Current tsdk typegen produces compile-time TypeScript types for structured output contracts but lacks robust runtime validators and streaming helpers. Customers build fragile runtime guards or copy patterns into their apps, causing parsing drift between SDK types and runtime checks. Streaming responses (partial JSON, function calling) make it hard to identify which union variant is being emitted until tokens complete; this ticket explores shape hints, incremental Zod refinements, and a small runtime helper layer to surface partial discriminants early.
goals: Emit Zod schema files alongside generated TypeScript types for every structured output contract
Emit JSON-Schema artifacts for customers who prefer schema-based validation and remote contract checking
Generate efficient runtime type guards (isX) for discriminated/sum types that work with streaming shape hints
Provide example streaming parsers that can yield partial discriminant values and a final validated object
Add docs and cookbook examples demonstrating common patterns (rerank, tool-calling, chat messages)
acceptance_criteria: tsdk codegen produces <name>.types.ts, <name>.zod.ts and <name>.schema.json for a sample contract
Generated Zod validators pass unit tests that mirror TypeScript type expectations (no false negatives on sample fixtures)
Runtime guards can detect discriminant value from streaming tokens in >80% of practical prompt fuzz cases in test harness
README examples for 'streaming-sumtype.md' and 'codegen-usage.md' merged into docs repo
No breaking changes for existing typegen users; opt-in flag --emit-runtime-schemas defaults to false for beta rollout
implementation_plan: Design: decide discriminant naming heuristics (tag, type, kind) and precedence if multiple present
Codegen changes: extend current tsdk codegen pipeline to optionally emit Zod definitions using generated AST
JSON-Schema: render Zod -> JSON-Schema or emit dedicated generator to preserve union tags and examples
Runtime helpers: implement streamingShapeHint API that takes token stream and emits early discriminant discovery events
Examples + tests: add a small example repo under experimental/tsdk-typegen-streaming with several prompts, fixtures, and property-based fuzz tests
Docs + changelog: add a migration guide and cookbook to docs.redwood.ai and add opt-in flag to CLI
technical_decisions: Prefer explicit 'tag' field by convention but fall back to 'type' and 'kind' in that order; documented as codegen heuristic
Use Zod for runtime validators to align with front-end ecosystems; generate Zod schemas programmatically rather than string templates
Emit JSON-Schema via zod-to-json-schema for compatibility but post-process to preserve discriminator mapping
Streaming shape hints will expose a minimal API: streamingShapeHint.onDiscriminant(value) and a parseReconcile(finalText) to validate full object
Keep --emit-runtime-schemas disabled by default (beta) to avoid expanding published artifact surface without opt-in
Avoid heavy runtime dependencies; the generated Zod helpers will require zod (peerDependency) and a small tsdk-runtime package for streaming helpers
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Beta): add feature behind CLI flag and e2e tests; publish internal alpha package
Phase 2 (Docs + Examples): publish cookbook and example repository; collect developer feedback via community channels
Phase 3 (Opt-in SDK): enable flag as CLI default for new projects; announce in release notes
Phase 4 (GA): flip default to on in a minor release after 2 weeks of opt-in telemetry and no major issues
qa_plan: Unit tests: generator output snapshot tests (TS, Zod, JSON-Schema)
Integration: run example prompts through the runtime streaming parser and compare to expected discriminant detection
Property tests: fuzz partial token sequences to assert streamingShapeHint recovers discriminant within a threshold
Cross-language smoke: ensure generated JSON-Schema validates with at least one non-Zod validator (ajv) in CI
test_cases: Simple union with explicit tag: { tag: 'ChoiceA', payload: { ... } } -> Zod and JSON-Schema generated
Union with implicit tag (type): codegen picks 'type' when 'tag' not present
Streaming partial JSON arrives in chunks: streamingShapeHint emits discriminant event before full parse and final reconcile succeeds
Malformed union payload triggers precise validation error with path and suggestion to retry with increased max_tokens
Backward compatibility: old generated types are still consumable when --emit-runtime-schemas is off
